note: Taught: the commission was set up to examine the constitutional system and suggest changes (Class 10 jess302; Class 8 hees202 says "to study constitutional reform").

Taught (WBBSE only): at the 1939 Tripuri session Subhas Bose defeated the Gandhi-nominated Pattabhi Sitaramayya and was elected president again (WBBSE Class VIII, PDF p. 518). NCERT does not mention Tripuri.

Taught: Gandhi began walking from Sabarmati on 12 March 1930 (Class 12 lehs303); 6 April 1930 is when the salt law was broken (NCERT and WBBSE PDF p. 492, which gives only 6 April). The chapter keeps both dates apart.
Not taught: the years in which the Swaraj Party contested council elections are not given in the NCERT or WBBSE sources; the chapter teaches only its founders and strategy.

Not taught. NCERT gives only the count (7 of 11 in Class 8, 8 of 11 in Class 12). WBBSE PDF p. 579 prints a sentence that reads "in the Muslim-majority provinces Punjab, Bengal, Assam, NWFP and Sind a Congress ministry was formed", which contradicts the official key (Punjab, no Congress ministry) and NCERT; it is probably a misprint of "was not formed". The chapter records the printed sentence in an exam_note and the official key stays authoritative.
Taught: the Dandi March began the Civil Disobedience Movement (Class 10 jess302).
Not in NCERT/WBBSE sources: the Kitchlew remark on Partition belongs to HIS-26 (the road to Partition).

Not taught, doubtful key. The official key of this WBCS (Exe.) Prelims 2016 paper is "Lahore" and stays authoritative. The NCERT sources only say the Lahore session (1929) declared Purna Swaraj and elected Nehru president; the pledge speaks of exploitation of the masses. They do not mention a "Social Democratic Resolution". The chapter has an exam_note saying this.

Taught (WBBSE only): in 1932 British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald's announcement spoke of the Communal Award (WBBSE PDF p. 576). NCERT only says "the British government conceded Ambedkar's demand". The question asks who declared it; the chapter answer is MacDonald.
Taught (WBBSE only): after resigning the presidency Subhas Bose formed the Forward Bloc (WBBSE Class VIII, PDF p. 518). Not in NCERT.
Taught: the Lahore session of 1929 declared Purna Swaraj (Complete Independence) as the goal.
Not taught by name: the chapter teaches Gandhi's campaign against untouchability and the name "harijan" (Class 10), but NCERT does not name the Harijan Sevak Sangh or its founder.
Not in the sources: the founding of AITUC and its first president are not in NCERT/WBBSE; belongs to a labour-movement topic outside this chapter.
Not in the sources: the Karachi 1931 resolution on Fundamental Rights is not in the NCERT sources used (Patel as Congress president in 1931 is, but not Karachi).
Not in the sources: the National Planning Committee is not in NCERT/WBBSE. Belongs to HIS-26 or the Indian Economy plan.
Not in the sources: Periyar and the Self-Respect Movement belong to the social-reform chapter (plan item 20); not in this chapter's sources.
Taught: the commission had no Indian member (Class 8 and Class 10).
Taught with a caveat: WBBSE (PDF pp. 585, 594) names A. K. Fazlul Huq as the leader of the Krishak Praja Party in Bengal. It does not use the word "founded"; no NCERT source.
Taught (WBBSE only): the Forward Bloc was formed by Subhas Bose (WBBSE Class VIII, PDF p. 518). Not in NCERT.
Not taught by name: the "All India Harijan Samaj" is not in NCERT; the chapter teaches only that Gandhi named the untouchables "harijan" and campaigned for temple entry and access to wells.
Taught: Purna Swaraj declared at the Lahore Congress, December 1929.
Not taught, doubtful key: the remark about Nehru and Jinnah is not in NCERT/WBBSE. The official key stays as it is; the chapter says nothing either way.
Not taught, doubtful key: the remark on the Simon Commission Report is not in NCERT/WBBSE (they say only that the commission was boycotted). The official key of the paper stays authoritative.
Taught: 6 April 1930, Gandhi reached Dandi and broke the salt law.

Taught with nuance: NCERT Class 8 - Iqbal in 1930 proposed a separate territory in the north-west within a federation, "not yet the precise idea of Pakistan"; Class 10 - his statement supposedly gave the intellectual justification. WBBSE (PDF p. 576) adds Choudhary Rahmat Ali, who "vaguely" mentioned the word Pakistan. Consistent with the official key (Iqbal); the chapter has an exam_note on the Iqbal/Rahmat Ali difference.
Taught: C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru founded the Swaraj Party (NCERT Class 10; WBBSE PDFs pp. 489-490).
Taught: Irwin was the Viceroy at the time of Dandi (NCERT says "Viceroy Irwin"; the option is "Lord Irwin").
Not in the sources: the inauguration of New Delhi (1931) is not in these NCERT/WBBSE texts.
Taught: the charkha is "the most abiding image of Indian nationalism" and a symbol of self-reliance (Class 12).
Not in the sources: the quotation is not in NCERT/WBBSE.
Taught: Dandi began the Civil Disobedience Movement.
Not in the sources: Churchill's remark on Gandhi is not in these texts.
Taught: Gandhi-Irwin Pact, 1931 (5 March in Class 10; 4 March in WBBSE PDF p. 498, "Delhi Pact"). The year is certain; the day differs between the books.
Not in the sources: the All India Kisan Sabha and its first president are not in these texts; belongs to a peasant-movements topic.
Taught: Vallabhbhai Patel led the Bardoli movement of 1928 (Class 8 hees202); Gandhi blessed it (Class 12).
Taught: Poona Pact, September 1932.
Not in the sources: the Self-Respect Movement and Periyar belong to the social-reform chapter (plan item 20).
Not taught: Das is taught as a Swaraj Party founder, but his "swaraj for the masses" formula is not in NCERT/WBBSE.
Not taught: WBBSE (PDF p. 494) mentions the young Rani Gidalo of the Naga area joining the revolt against British rule, but neither source says who gave her the title "Rani".
Not in the sources: the Vaikkom Satyagraha is not in these texts (temple-entry movements in the south, plan item 20).
Not in the sources: Abul Kalam Azad as youngest Congress president (age 35) is not in the texts used.
Not in the sources: the National Planning Committee of 1938 is not in NCERT/WBBSE. Belongs to HIS-26.
Not taught: the chapter teaches the Nehru Report (dominion status, 1928) and Lahore 1929 (Purna Swaraj), but no source states that the report was shelved at Lahore.
Not in the sources: no mediator of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact is named in these texts.
Not in the sources: the Khaksar movement is not in these texts.
Not in the sources: the book "Gandhi versus Lenin" is not in these texts.
Not in the sources: the "Two Mahatmas" remark is not in these texts (Sarojini Naidu herself is taught).
Not in the sources: Iqbal at the Second and Third Round Table Conferences is not stated (the chapter teaches his 1930 Allahabad presidential address).

Taught (WBBSE): Abdul Ghaffar Khan, a follower of Gandhi, was also known as "Frontier Gandhi" (WBBSE PDF p. 494). NCERT calls him a devout disciple of Gandhi, arrested in April 1930 (Peshawar), without the nickname.
